chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him, 'How is tayammum?' He said, 'It is one striking for wudu (ablution) and for ghusl from janabah. You strike with your two hands twice, then shake them off once: once for the face and once for the hands. And whenever you find water, then ghusl is upon you if you are junub, and wudu (ablution) if you are not junub.'

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمُ: dry ablution performed in place of ritual washing
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ritual bath required in certain states of impurity
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, whose availability restores the obligation of normal purification
key_terms.الْوَجْهِ: the face, one of the areas wiped in tayammum
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution) required for ritual purity before acts such as salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْيَدَيْنِ: the hands, one of the areas wiped in tayammum
key_terms.نَفْضَةً: a shaking off of the hands after striking the earth

ai.seo_question: How is tayammum performed for wudu (ablution) and ghusl in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the method of tayammum and distinguishes its use for wudu (ablution) and ghusl due to janabah. It also states that when water becomes available, one must perform ghusl if in janabah, or wudu (ablution) if not.
